name: Ferrotex-M
description: Ferrotex-M is a CNT composite material produced by Crucible Industries in which iron-nickel magnetic nanoparticles are uniformly distributed along and within multi-wall carbon nanotube walls during a chemical vapor deposition process, creating a material with both structural CNT properties and tunable magnetic behavior. The magnetic response can be set during manufacture to produce soft-magnetic, hard-magnetic, or magnetically-shielding variants from the same base feedstock. Ferrotex-M is the material of choice wherever structural components must also manage magnetic fields — motors, generators, and electromagnetic containment systems.
applications: electric motor rotor and stator components
story_hooks: Ferrotex-M's magnetic shielding variant is being used to line a hidden facility — nothing electronic can detect what's inside, and that's exactly the point.
Crucible Industries has a monopoly on the iron-nickel nanoparticle feedstock; a competitor is trying to break that monopoly through means that aren't entirely legal.
A shipment of Ferrotex-M intended for medical MRI shielding has been diverted — the material would make an excellent liner for a room where augmented individuals can't be scanned or tracked.
